author: reek
body: `ImapClient` had never compiled, and the reason it had never compiled is the reason it needed this test: nothing cites it that anything else cites, so no battery run ever asked it to build. A chapter nobody compiles accumulates defects at leisure, and this one had two beyond the twelve that stopped the lexer.

author: reek
body: And the alphabet is the other half. `imap-text-to-bytes` used `char-code-at` alone, which answers the CCE code point: `A` is 41 in CCE and 65 on the wire. Every command this chapter framed, and every XOAUTH2 credential it base64-encoded, was in the wrong alphabet. A round-trip through our own encoder cannot see that -- both halves agree on CCE -- so the expected bytes below are written out as the ASCII a reader can check against the RFC, and `65` on the first byte is the whole point of the line.

author: reek
body: Three commands rather than one, because they differ in what they interpolate: a bare command, one carrying a caller's mailbox name, and one carrying a number rendered by `show`. A conversion that handled literals and dropped interpolated text would pass on the first alone.
